ObjectName.value: Elephant Rock and surf shed, Currumbin Beach, Queensland, Australia

Categories.value: Gold Coast, Queensland|Elephant Rock|1959 in Queensland|Files with coordinates missing SDC location of creation|Currumbin Beach|Bain-O'Gorman Collection (QUT)

ImageDescription.value: The rock formation, called Elephant Rock, was once covered in vines and coastal flowers and was named Green Rock by early European settlers and visitors. In early photographs, the rock resembles an elephant sitting on the beach facing out to sea and, over time the name Green Rock was no longer used and the alternative name of Elephant Rock replaced it. The rock shelf surrounding Elephant Rock on its protected northern side was chosen by the local surf club as an ideal location to build a small hut as a clubhouse. Over many decades the clubhouse was often damaged by high tides and cyclones, but the tenacity of the Vikings Currumbin Surf Lifesaving Club membership to maintain their position on the rocky shelf has resulted in the original club house expanding and becoming one of the most popular locations on the Gold Coast for dining and entertainment. (https://www.goldcoaststories.com.au/elephant-rock/)

ObjectName.value: Andamane Nil Island Five Beach

Categories.value: Neil Island|Self-published work|Beaches of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands|India photographs taken on 2004-12-27|2004 tsunami on the Andaman and Nicobar Islands

ImageDescription.value: Fotografia scattata sull'isola di Shaheed (Neil Island), isole Andamane, India, il 27 dicembre 2004 dopo che un violentissimo terremoto, con una magnitudo di 9,1 ha colpito l'Oceano Indiano al largo della costa nord-occidentale di Sumatra in Indonesia. Le isole andamane e le isole Nicobare furono travolte dallo tsunami che si generò dopo il terremoto provocando, si stima, circa 8000 vittime. Molte isole vennero inondate, l'Isola di Neil Island fu colpita solo in parte, soprattutto nel versante esposto verso l'Indonesia. La fotografia ritrae la spiaggia di Five Beach sul versante orientale, che guarda l'indonesia, tra le aree colpite dell'isola, in cui molti detriti furono portati dal mare sulla spiaggia
